description: hyper v1.12.0 tests/server.rs (chunk1): GET body handling, response_body_lengths::*, custom reason phrase, keep-alive after a chunked response, POST Content-Length. All assertions in these tests run on the test's main thread (no unjoined client threads). The serve() fixture's serve_connection(..).await.unwrap() runs in a spawned task whose panic is never observed, so no case asserts the connection outcome.

cases.name: get_should_ignore_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture, default reply. hyper asserts: one read() of up to 256 bytes returns Ok (an RST or a 1 s timeout would fail the unwrap; Ok(0) would pass), and server.body() == b"" (the first body the TestService read). The bytes after the head are not body (GET without Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding) and, with Connection: close, are not parsed as a second request (not asserted).

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

I shouldn't be read.

cases.name: get_with_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture, default reply. hyper asserts: one read() of up to 256 bytes returns Ok, and server.body() == "I'm a good request." (19 bytes: Content-Length frames the GET body, the trailing CRLF is not body). What the server does with the leftover CRLF on the keep-alive connection is not asserted.

steps.data:

cases.notes:
run_test (tests/server.rs:94-178): GET HTTP/1.1 with Connection: close, read_to_string to EOF. body.find("

").unwrap() -> contains CRLFCRLF. has_header = substring of the text before the first CRLFCRLF -> scope head. expects_chunked=false: no 'transfer-encoding:' and no 'chunked

Port decision: the not_contains checks add ci:true (hyper's check is case-sensitive; ci is stricter and states the intent that no such header appears in any case; hyper passes both).

cases.name: response_body_lengths::chunked_response_known
cases.notes:
run_test (tests/server.rs:94-178), see fixed_response_known. Reply: transfer-encoding: chunked header with a Known body 'foo bar baz' (hyper keeps the user's TE header although the length is known). Asserts: CRLFCRLF present; head has 'transfer-encoding:' and 'chunked
', no 'content-length:'. Chunk layout (n = index after the head): body[n+1..n+3] == CRLF (one-character size line), body[n+3..len-7] == 'foo bar baz', body[len-7..] == '
0

'; the after_head regex encodes exactly these three slices (hex case and digit value are not checked). not_contains check adds ci:true (port decision). Pilot case from the harness author, kept; added the CRLFCRLF and ci checks. Applies to every chunked case in this file: has_header() searches only the text before the first CRLFCRLF, so 'chunked
' is found only if the transfer-encoding line is not the last header line. hyper writes date last (role.rs encode_headers), so its TE line is never last. A server that writes TE as the last header line fails hyper's assertion and this case, although its response is valid HTTP.

cases.name: response_body_lengths::te_response_adds_chunked
cases.notes:
run_test (tests/server.rs:94-178), see fixed_response_known and chunked_response_known. Reply: transfer-encoding: gzip header (body not actually gzipped), Unknown body 'foo bar baz'. The server must add chunked as the final transfer coding (hyper writes 'transfer-encoding: gzip, chunked'; only the substrings below are asserted). Asserts: CRLFCRLF present; head has 'transfer-encoding:' and 'chunked
', no 'content-length:'; chunked body layout as in chunked_response_known. not_contains check adds ci:true (port decision). Observed on the reference (not asserted by hyper): the head is 'transfer-encoding: gzip, chunked
connection: close, chunked
': role.rs encode_headers never resets must_write_chunked, so the next multi-valued field written by the same code path (here the connection: close hyper adds for the request's Connection: close) also gets ', chunked' appended. Diff mode compares these bytes.

cases.name: get_response_custom_reason_phrase
cases.notes:
serve() fixture. Reply: reason phrase 'Cool' (hyper::ext::ReasonPhrase), status 200, empty body. Read to EOF (Connection: close). hyper asserts with str::lines(): the first line is 'HTTP/1.1 200 Cool'; after skipping to the first empty line, that line exists and nothing follows it. expect[0] is an exact transcription of that lines() check: str::lines() splits at LF and strips one CR before it, so a line is empty iff its bytes before the LF are '' or '', and a non-empty line is 2+ bytes or 1 byte other than CR; the regex is: status line, LF-terminated non-empty lines, one empty line, end of input. It rejects responses that the SPEC 14 mapping alone accepts: an empty line inside the head before the first CRLFCRLF, e.g. 'X: a

Y: b

' or 'Y: b


' (hyper fails both; checked with a Rust transcription of the assertions). expect[1..3] are the SPEC 14 mapping (starts_with the status line + CRLF, CRLFCRLF present, nothing after the head). Port decision: expect[1..3] require CRLF line ends, which lines() does not (it accepts a bare LF); hyper writes CRLF and RFC 9112 2.1 requires CRLF from senders.

cases.name: get_chunked_response_with_ka
cases.notes:
serve() fixture. Request 1 (Connection: keep-alive); reply 1: transfer-encoding: chunked, Known body 'foo bar baz'. read_until (8192-byte buffer) the received bytes end with '
foo bar baz
0

'. Request 2 on the same socket (Connection: close); reply 2: content-length: 8, body 'zar quux'. read_until the bytes end with 'zar quux'. hyper queues reply 2 after reading response 1; queuing both up front is equivalent (SPEC 5.2). The connection must stay open after the chunked response; an EOF before 'zar quux' fails the read_until (hyper's read_until would spin on Ok(0) and never finish).

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: keep-alive

GET /quux HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

cases.name: post_with_content_length_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture, default reply. Request has NO Host header (hyper accepts an HTTP/1.1 request without Host; RFC 9112 3.2 says a server MUST answer 400, so this case pins hyper's lenient behavior). hyper asserts: one read() of up to 256 bytes returns Ok, and server.body() == 'hello'.

steps.data:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Length: 5

hello

cases.name: post_with_invalid_prefix_content_length
cases.notes: serve() fixture. 'Content-Length: +5' is not 1*DIGIT, so the head is a parse error and the server answers 400. hyper asserts: one read() into a zeroed 256-byte buffer returns Ok, and its first 26 bytes == 'HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\n' (so the read must return at least those 26 bytes). The rest of the response and the connection outcome are not asserted.

POST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Length: +5

hello
